name: Sterling-Nakamura Executive Defense Pistol EDP-1 'Handshake'
description: An ultra-compact ceramic pistol designed to pass through standard security scanning systems undetected. The EDP-1 is constructed entirely from non-metallic materials — ceramic barrel, polymer frame, carbon-fiber internals — and fires caseless ceramic-tipped rounds that are similarly invisible to metal detectors. The weapon holds 4 rounds, has an effective range of 10 meters, and is designed to be concealed within a briefcase, jacket lining, or even a prosthetic limb compartment. Sterling-Nakamura issues it to senior executives as a last-resort personal defense weapon, though its obvious utility as an assassination tool in secured environments has made it the most sought-after concealable weapon in GLMZ.
specifications: caliber: 5mm caseless ceramic-tipped magazine: 4 rounds effective range: 3-10 meters construction: 100% non-metallic — ceramic, polymer, carbon fiber detectability: Passes standard metal detection and basic material scanning weight: 0.18 kg form factor: Credit card width, 12 cm length barrel life: 20 rounds before ceramic degradation
story_hooks: A diplomat was shot dead in a Tier 4 secured conference room that had passed full security screening — the only weapon that could have entered is an EDP-1, narrowing the suspect pool to people with Sterling-Nakamura executive access.
A 3D printing schematic for an EDP-1 replica has been uploaded to the open net — the replicas are fragile and inaccurate, but they pass the same security scans.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively elegant, almost minimalist pistol that resembles a high-end personal device more than a weapon. Its flat, rectangular profile and credit-card-thin dimensions give it the appearance of a premium tech accessory — something you'd expect in a corpo executive's briefcase rather than a lethal instrument.
physical_description.dimensions: 12 cm length, 3.2 cm width, 1.8 cm depth at grip; barrel bore approximately 5mm
physical_description.weight_description: Feather-light and perfectly balanced — 180 grams feels almost insubstantial in the palm, more like holding a thick piece of composite material than a firearm. The low mass creates an unsettling disconnect between its lethality and its gossamer feel.
physical_description.primary_material: Ceramic barrel core, reinforced polymer frame, carbon-fiber internal mechanisms and trigger assembly. No steel, no ferrous metals anywhere in the construction.
physical_description.finish: Satin-smooth ceramic surfaces with subtle translucent quality — almost opalescent under light. The polymer sections are finished in a pearl-white or deep charcoal matte, designed to blend with luxury corporate aesthetics.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte ceramic white or charcoal black. Accent colors: subtle brushed-titanium-colored polymer trim along the grip and slide rails, minimal branding in gunmetal gray.
physical_description.grip_texture: Finely textured polymer with a grip-enhancing microtexture reminiscent of premium smartphone casings — soft-touch, non-reflective, with subtle diamond-pattern knurling for index finger purchase.
distinctive_features: Integrated safety lever recessed flush into the frame — barely visible unless you know where to look
Minimalist rear sight notch machined into the ceramic slide itself — no protruding elements
Loading port positioned along the grip spine for ceramic-round insertion, sealed with a sliding polymer latch
Faint Sterling-Nakamura logo embossed — not engraved — into the grip, blending seamlessly with the material
Barrel port has a barely-perceptible flare at the muzzle, designed for ceramic-round stabilization
Micro-texture finish throughout to defeat fingerprint and reflection detection
Ultra-thin trigger guard, barely a finger's width, integrated into the frame profile
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura corporate logo (subtle embossed mark, not stamped) on the left grip panel. Serial number laser-etched on the interior of the slide in micro-print, invisible from external view. No visible caliber or warning markings.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when issued — these weapons are regularly maintained by corporate security teams and rarely see heavy use. When fielded, they show minimal wear due to their material composition. Well-maintained examples appear almost new; heavily used examples may show micro-scratches on ceramic surfaces and slight ceramic degradation at the barrel crown.
